sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Apex Ecotech Limited; NSE SME; ISIN INE0T4V01015. Research cutoff 2026-10-20. Dated quote ₹252.95 on 2026-10-19, not a live executable bid. Five-year nominal INR scenarios use a 15% analyst equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh illustrative position. Current scope and capital bridge are described in financial forensics and the linked model.

Gate conclusions: G 1 Integrity: No critical integrity failure established; pay ceilings, related remuneration and concentrated control require monitoring. G 2 Financial reliability: Deposit reclassifications reconciled; audits unmodified. Provisional invoicing is not substituted for audited sales. G 3 Funding: Low debt and credit cushion support base; linked stress funds ordinary WC and guarantee collateral separately. G 4 Tradability: All 60 sessions observed, but ESM-I, lot 202360 rupees and no live spread require conservative execution.

Evidence confidence: historical_financials: high after deposit classification bridge; economic_growth: medium; project execution supported, no current physical throughput or customer-share table; governance: medium; actual future pay unknown; valuation: medium conditional inputs, substantial forecast uncertainty. Forecast uncertainty is distinct from accuracy of the underlying disclosures.

Official 2026-10-19 close ₹252.95; volume 2,400.0 shares, turnover ₹601,560, 3.0 trades, lot 800, series ['ST']. This dated trade is not a live executable bid. 20-session mean/median daily turnover ₹3,894,174/₹3,370,140; conservative denominator is the lower. ₹5 lakh theoretical exit takes 7.42/2.97/1.48 sessions at 2%/5%/10% participation before whole-lot rounding. 60-session mean/median daily turnover ₹3,489,687/₹2,825,360; conservative denominator is the lower. ₹5 lakh theoretical exit takes 8.85/3.54/1.77 sessions at 2%/5%/10% participation before whole-lot rounding. Not an exit guarantee: spreads, available bids, circuits, impact, settlement/surveillance and whole-lot minimum positions remain to be checked. [M1]

Official named surveillance list matches: Enhanced Surveillance Measure (ESM) - Stage I as of 20-Oct-2026. This is a trading/surveillance constraint, not a finding of misconduct. Liquidity estimates cannot assume unconstrained execution; verify applicable stage rules, circuits, settlement and live bid depth.

Official October 19 EOD indicators, effective next trading session October 21: ESM Stage I; Less than 100 unique PAN traded in previous 30 days; SME scrip is not regularly traded. These cautions do not contradict the actual observed turnover history: generic irregular-trading status is not evidence of any particular missing session. PAN breadth and expired mandatory market-making can weaken executable depth even when daily turnover is present. [REG1][REGFMT]

Current implementation assessment L 6: All 60 sessions observed: conservative median 2.82536 m rupees gives 3.54 days to exit 5 lakh at 5%, starting 7; downgrade 1 for ESM-I,202360 rupee lot, only 3 trades October 19 and unobserved spread.2% participation 8.85 days; whole-lot execution differs from fractional reference position. The decoded exchange cautions are incorporated as implementation risks, not invented zero-turnover days. Existing conservative downgrade already covers restricted depth/lot/surveillance risk; no automatic repeated penalty for correlated alerts.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Water/wastewater solutions provider listed NSE Emerge 4 December 2024; Indian GAAP/AS financials. FY 26/FY 25 revenue ₹148.6507/70.9553 cr and PAT ₹17.0230/8.5608 cr. EPS ₹12.91/7.91 grew less because FY 26 uses the larger IPO share base for the full year. This dilution normalization is not operational deterioration. [S1]

Goods revenue 146.5464 cr and services 2.1043 cr make service share 1.42%; do not label all revenue recurring O&M. Auditor KAM tests goods dispatch/customer acceptance and service completion, not automatic order-book recognition. Historical top 10 FY 24 concentration 79.76%, top 1 12.74%; latest quantified shares not located. June L&T revision increases scope from 45–55 cr to 55–67 cr, rather than adding the entire revised value to old backlog. March 125 cr and July 146 cr backlog snapshots must not be summed. July 34 cr Q 1 invoicing is expressly provisional/unreviewed. [S1][DRHP][LOI][JUL]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: EMS FY 26 consolidated revenue 732.7472 cr versus 972.4919 cr and PAT 91.1943 cr versus 183.7835 cr illustrate that water-sector demand does not remove execution cyclicality. EMS has municipal, network and HAM exposure; Apex is smaller industrial systems engineering. This is an operating-risk comparison, not evidence for copying a P/E. No precisely matched listed twin or current peer-multiple target is asserted. [PEER1]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Comparable FY 23–26 revenue 34.5738→53.0809→70.9553→148.6507 cr yields 62.6% CAGR, starting 9; medium economic-growth confidence caps 8. Five annual observations include FY 22 revenue 19.5118 cr. Named project scope and dispatch/acceptance recognition support real execution, but current customer concentration and physical throughput are not separately quantified.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: March cash 35.0594 cr contains 23.4636 cr guarantee-margin deposits. Model excludes restricted deposits from excess cash and funds future collateral explicitly. Net income-tax asset 0.8293 cr is excluded, not confused with gross 5.8612 cr provision payable on top of 6.6905 cr advances. Disputed MSME interest 0.2017 cr plus GST demands 0.1798 cr less predeposit 0.0084 cr enter conservative settlement reserve; MSME principal 0.032 cr already in payables is not duplicated. Deleted income-tax demand is not reserved again. DLF claim 0.4749 cr includes interest/damages, but only 0.1188 cr receivable is carried; vendor litigation 0.0428 cr is separately within advances. These small known matters do not constitute a critical integrity hold. FY 26 operating EBIT 21.5584 cr versus 10.8407 cr; standardized 25% NOPAT 16.1688 cr divided by average equity-plus-debt 55.48825 cr gives 29.14%. Incremental 8.038275 cr NOPAT/18.1533 cr capital is 44.28%, but IPO timing and expanding guarantee deposits mean these are accounting proxies, not cash project IRR. Low fixed capital is offset by collateral and vendor funding. [S1]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
CRISIL 31 July rationale assignsBBB/Stable/A 3+ on₹75 cr ratedbankfacilities. July 1 unexecutedorders₹146 cr support visibility, but tenders and competition constrain pricing. FY 26 GCA days 137 versus 237, debtors 64 versus 114 andinventory 13 versus 15 show improved intensity despite absolute cashuse. Banklimitutilization 17% in 12 months toJune and₹0.3 cr annualtermobligations support funding resilience; ₹17–23 crfuturecashaccrual is a projection, not CFO. This counterevidence moderates the cashfactor to 5(mixed), rather than 4(recurringweakness), while low cumulativeconversion and vendoradvances still prevent a highscore. [U1]

Current audit/IFC unmodified and related remuneration transparent, but family control 69.29%, three directors paid 2.6915 cr and spouses 0.2091 cr merit scrutiny. May EGM approved 7.5 cr aggregate director ceilings versus actual 2.6915 cr. It is a ceiling, not proven extraction;100 cr borrowing/section 186 approvals likewise are permissions, not balances. Same auditor reappointed, not resignation. Directors themselves and related spouses are identified in Note 20; names of connected enterprises are not proof of transactions absent amounts. May approved option plan covers 220000 shares, two-to-five-year vesting and grant-date pricing. No actual grant or option proceeds are invented. [S1][APR][VOTE][AUD]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY 26/FY 25 CFO ₹6.7668/−5.2420 cr; capex ₹1.9632/0.1008 cr; FCF proxies ₹4.8036/−5.3428 cr. Two-year CFO/PAT = 1.5248/25.5838 = 0.060. FY 26 short-term loans/advances absorbed ₹9.5881 cr and receivables ₹5.1893 cr. Deposit movement of ₹13.9529 cr is investing, distinct from operating conversion. Restricted deposits are excluded in the linked model, with future collateral funded explicitly. [S1]

FY 24 DRHP CFO 5.9404 cr plus 0.7463 cr FD release equals FY 25 report comparative 6.6867 cr; FY 25 old CFO−14.0802 cr plus 8.8382 cr FD investment equals revised−5.2420 cr. Reclassification reconciles total cash and is not unexplained misstatement. Comparable FY 22–26 CFO 0.4520/3.4883/5.9404/−5.2420/6.7668 cr versus PAT−0.6586/3.5210/6.6304/8.5608/17.0230 cr gives 32.52% cumulative conversion. FY 26 capex 1.9632 cr, cash after capex 4.8036 cr precedes 13.9529 cr additional restricted deposits. The latter is a real funding need even if outside CFO. [S1][H25][DRHP]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Base/bear/bull five-year IRRs 13.08%/-18.33%/28.69%; terminal prices 467.71/91.90/892.88 rupees. Base 15% hurdle entry 232.53. Annual linked schedules fund vendor/receivable WC, guarantee collateral, capex, taxes, debt interest and dilution. These are conditional estimates, not targets or buy instructions. Pay-ceiling, cash-loss, tax-refund and current-share sensitivities accompany them. [S1][APR][VOTE][M1] Model correction, 20 October 2026: our earlier model omitted opening claims. The revised reference settles ₹0.0000000 crore at opening and deducts ₹0.7644000 crore of remaining net legacy employee obligations at terminal. These are corrections to our calculations, not changes to issuer-reported data. Future service expense remains funded through forecast margins. Accelerated settlement gives base return 13.0807% versus the reference 13.0807%. BQS, GQS, IAS and classification are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Analyst stress: project milestones are delayed, retention and vendor advances remain outstanding, and guarantees absorb liquidity while delivery costs continue. Monitor order-to-revenue-to-billing-to-cash reconciliation, unbilled assets, top customer concentration, retention duration, performance guarantees and commissioning outcomes. Water-demand growth alone does not establish pricing power.

Bear terminal price 91.90 and severe 18.30 show material capital impairment despite low opening debt. Guarantee lockup and project margin stress are funded explicitly, not ignored.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-times and ten-times October 19 price require 1264.75 and 2529.50 rupees. At 20 x terminal earnings and 1.34052 cr potential shares, required earnings are 84.77/169.54 cr, versus 17.023 cr current PAT. At 10% PAT margin this implies sales 848/1695 cr and major incremental guarantee/working-capital funding. Not a supported base case. [S1][APR][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Test order-to-invoice-to-acceptance-to-cash reconciliation, vendor advances, statutory assets and restricted-deposit intensity. Track actual director pay against new ceilings, option grants and shareholder dilution; refresh guarantee terms and cash availability. A sustained collection deterioration or margin decline outside funded stress invalidates the thesis; an improving cash record could justify higher CASH/CAP scores. No live spread or executable bid is available. [S1][APR][CALL][M1]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Industrial water-system execution is scaling with low financial debt, but guarantee collateral consumes most reported cash and cumulative operating conversion is weak. Approved pay ceilings and customer concentration require scrutiny. Conditional funded valuation is available without treating restricted deposits as distributable cash. All canonical factors supported and calculated; REV capped 8 for medium economic-growth confidence, no automatic cash override. Conditional IAS includes collateral funding and full potential option dilution.

Final published measures: BQS 5.9; GQS 6.85; IAS 5.125. Any change in price, funded cash deployment, share count or execution restrictions requires recomputation; these are conditional research classifications, not a trade instruction.
